\worksheethead

\vspace{8pt}


\typehead{Telescoping Sums}{Find a closed form for the $n$th partial sum $s_n$ (use partial fractions or log rules), then determine whether the series converges by computing $\lim_{n\to+\infty} s_n$. If it converges, find its sum.}

\problem{1.}{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{k^{2}+3k+2} = \frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{20} + \cdots + \frac{1}{k^{2}+3k+2} + \cdots}

\divider

\problem{2.}{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{(2k-1)(2k+1)} = \frac{1}{1\cdot 3} + \frac{1}{3\cdot 5} + \frac{1}{5\cdot 7} + \cdots + \frac{1}{(2k-1)(2k+1)} + \cdots}

\divider

\problem{3.}{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \ln\!\left(\frac{k}{k+1}\right) = \ln\frac12 + \ln\frac23 + \ln\frac34 + \cdots + \ln\!\left(\frac{k}{k+1}\right) + \cdots}

\divider

\problem{4.}{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{2}{k(k+2)} = \frac{2}{1\cdot 3} + \frac{2}{2\cdot 4} + \frac{2}{3\cdot 5} + \cdots + \frac{2}{k(k+2)} + \cdots}

\divider

\problem{5.}{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{4}{k^{2}+4k+3} = \frac{4}{2\cdot 4} + \frac{4}{3\cdot 5} + \frac{4}{4\cdot 6} + \cdots + \frac{4}{k^{2}+4k+3} + \cdots}

\divider

\problem{6.}{\frac{1}{4\cdot 5} + \frac{1}{5\cdot 6} + \frac{1}{6\cdot 7} + \cdots + \frac{1}{(k+3)(k+4)} + \cdots}

\divider

\problem{7.}{\frac{1}{1\cdot 4} + \frac{1}{4\cdot 7} + \frac{1}{7\cdot 10} + \cdots + \frac{1}{(3k-2)(3k+1)} + \cdots}
